run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:35:11Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by the proxy's own failures: its ingress and router-egress spans carry error=true and http.status_code=500, and its access log records POST /api/checkout returning 500. The failing trace shows the 500 is generated upstream of the proxy: frontend POST /api/checkout → checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code 13, message '13 INTERNAL: shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500') → shipping /get-quote (ERROR 'Internal Server Error', 5.001 s) → shipping outbound 'POST quote' span (ERROR 'Timeout', 5.001 s). The error rate in this path jumped from a 0.0037–0.0185/s span-error baseline to 0.078/s at 00:36:11 and ~0.9/s from 00:40:11 onward. The only change that coincides with the onset is a chaos-mesh fault injection: events show Schedule chaos-mesh/otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition spawning a NetworkChaos object every minute from 00:35:05, each 'Applied' to pods otel-demo/quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w and otel-demo/shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv and each reaching TimeUp/Recovered ~1 minute later — the first application at 00:35:05 matches the minute the frontend-proxy error rate began to rise. All otel-demo pods are Running, ready with 0 restarts, and no flagd fault flag is enabled, so pod crash and feature-flag causes are not supported. Conclusion is partial because the causal object is evidenced only by chaos-mesh events (the Schedule/NetworkChaos resources themselves cannot be read with the permitted kinds), the email-side 500 is not directly observed, and the alert's exact expression/0.6444 value could not be reproduced from the available metrics.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own spans fail: for service_name="frontend-proxy", span_name="ingress" with status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" the rate was 0.0111/s at the 00:35:00 sample, 0.429/s at 00:39:00 and 0.44–0.49/s through the 00:48:00 sample; span_name="router frontend egress" ERROR went from 0/s at 00:35:00 to 0.44–0.49/s from 00:39:00 onward, while the UNSET (no-status) rates for the same two operations stayed ~9.1–10.6/s.

Compared with its own pre-incident baseline, frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate was 0.0037–0.0185/s in the samples from 00:12:11 to 00:35:11, then 0.0778/s at 00:36:11, 0.526/s at 00:38:11 and 0.907/s at 00:40:11.

Error spans appear in the checkout chain and in no other frontend operations: for the 00:30:00–00:52:37 window, checkout span_names "oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder" and "HTTP POST", shipping span_names "/get-quote" and "POST quote", frontend "POST /api/checkout" and frontend-proxy "ingress"/"router frontend egress" all move from 0 to roughly 0.45–0.49 errors/s, while frontend "GET /api/cart", "GET /api/data", "grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart" and "grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" stay at 0 throughout.

The frontend-proxy container's access log for 00:34:00–00:52:37 contains 312 lines matching HTTP 5xx; the newest 15 (00:44:30–00:45:05) are all '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream' with upstream service 'frontend', 21-byte responses and 5.0–5.7 s upstream times, plus one '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO.

Whole trace 57075df3f14f46a92d8ea1cf5a6dbdd0 attributes the proxy 500 to the checkout path: load-generator user_checkout_single → frontend-proxy "ingress" and "router frontend egress" (error=true, http.status_code=500, ~5.33 s) → frontend "POST /api/checkout" (500) → frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code 13) → checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (ERROR, 13) with exception message '13 INTERNAL: shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500' → checkout "HTTP POST" (ERROR) → shipping "/get-quote" (ERROR, otel.status_description 'Internal Server Error', 5.001 s) → shipping "POST quote" (ERROR, otel.status_description 'Timeout', 5.001 s).

A sample of shipping error spans shows the same 5-second signature repeatedly: shipping "/get-quote" spans of ~5.001 s with otel.status_description 'Internal Server Error', each having a child shipping "POST quote" span of ~5.001 s with otel.status_description 'Timeout' (e.g. trace 57075df3f14f46a92d8ea1cf5a6dbdd0 at start_us 1794962784254605).

Chaos-mesh events name the recurring fault injection: kind Schedule, namespace chaos-mesh, name otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition emitted "Spawned ... Create new object: otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-9xnx8" at 00:35:05 and one Spawned per minute through otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-5czjs at 00:44:05; the spawned NetworkChaos objects logged '"Applied", Normal, Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w' and 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv' at 00:35:05, 00:36:05, ... 00:44:05, each followed about 55 s later by TimeUp and 'Successfully recover chaos' for the same two pods.

All 21 pods in namespace otel-demo, including frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-wvxht, checkout-5dccddf8bb-pd7qk, shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv, quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w and email-59f69bc6cf-8z5c5, are phase Running, container ready 'true' and restart count 0, with startTimes on 2026-11-17T23:58:22–23:58:24Z.
The chaos machinery itself is running and ready in namespace chaos-mesh: three chaos-controller-manager-fc8878644-* pods and four chaos-daemon-* pods, all ready with 0 restarts.

quote and email emit no error statuses: for service_name=~"quote|email" the only series returned over 00:30–00:52 carry status_code="STATUS_CODE_UNSET" (quote: POST /getquote, calculate-quote, {closure}; email: POST /send_order_confirmation, send_email, sinatra.render_template), and their rates fall from ~0.556/s at 00:35:00 to ~0.09/s at 00:45–00:49 and 0 at 00:52:00; no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was returned for either service.

quote's server-side handling was fast and error-free in the sampled requests: in traces at 00:43:58–00:44:02 the quote spans POST /getquote completed in 225–318 µs, {closure} in 135–181 µs and calculate-quote in 22–28 µs with no error status, and in one of those traces checkout POST /api/checkout returned http.status_code 200 after 2.33 s.

The newest 60 of the 108 log lines read from container quote in pod quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w (spanning 00:36:00.387–00:45:00.947) are all the literal line 'Calculated quote'; the container has no previous instance and the read reached 00:45:00, after which no lines were available.

No feature-flag fault is enabled by configuration: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config key demo.flagd.json defines 12 flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure), all with defaultVariant "off".

The late-window decline is a volume effect, not a recovery signal: total frontend-proxy span rate was 20.4/s at 00:35:00, 19.4/s at 00:48:00, then 15.5/s at 00:49:00, 10.7/s at 00:50:00, 6.2/s at 00:51:00 and 0 at 00:52:00, so all series on the service decay together at the end of the sampled range.

frontend-proxy is not failing on its own account at the object level (pod Running, ready, 0 restarts), and in the failing trace the calls to cart (oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, rpc.grpc.status_code 0), currency (Currency/Convert, otel.status_code OK) and product-catalog (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, rpc.grpc.status_code 0) all succeeded; the 500 is raised further down the chain at shipping /get-quote.

Feature-flag-driven fault injection (e.g. a fault flag such as emailMemoryLeak or paymentFailure switched on in flagd) is not supported: every flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config has defaultVariant "off". Runtime flagd overrides are not visible from the ConfigMap and were not checked.

The recurring network partition applied by chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition to pods quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w and shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv (first Applied 00:35:05, repeated every minute) is what makes the shipping→quote leg time out at exactly 5.0 s and return 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500', which propagates as checkout PlaceOrder INTERNAL, frontend POST /api/checkout 500 and finally frontend-proxy 500s — i.e. the alert's trigger.

The 'expected 200, got 500' part of the shipping/checkout error text suggests the failing leg is quote's HTTP POST to the email service, but the email side is unverified: email spans carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET, an email trace search for http.status_code="500" matched nothing, and the email container produced no log lines in the window.

Have the chaos-mesh owner read and, if this is not intended load, suspend Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition (namespace chaos-mesh) to confirm the causal test: the frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate should return to its pre-00:35 baseline of 0.0037–0.0185/s.

Instrument the email service's HTTP status and latency (its spans currently record no status and its container logs nothing in the window) so the 'expected 200, got 500' response attributed to the email call can be verified rather than inferred.

gaps: The chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition and the spawned NetworkChaos objects could not be read: chaos-mesh custom resources are not among the readable kinds, so the selector, direction, target pairs, duration and current phase of the partition, and the time the Schedule was created, are unverified; the cause rests on events only.

No alerting rules are loaded in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules returned nothing for rule_name RequestErrorRate and nothing for type=alert, so the alert expression and its annotated value 0.6444444444444444 could not be reproduced; the traces-derived frontend-proxy error-span share in this window is a few percent of spans, not 0.644, so the metric the rule evaluates is unknown.

The email service (pod email-59f69bc6cf-8z5c5) produced no log lines in the window, its spans carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and a trace search for http.status_code="500" on service email returned no traces, so the HTTP 500 that shipping reports from the email call is not directly observed.

A log query against pod quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w for error|fail|500|email|Exception over 00:34:00–00:52:37 returned nothing, but that view has status no_data and is therefore not evidence of absence; quote error output is unknown.

Coverage after ~00:45 is limited: quote logs end at 00:45:00, frontend-proxy logs at 00:45:10, and all span-rate series decay to 0 by 00:52:00 together with total volume, so whether the failures continued past ~00:48 and whether the chaos Schedule was still spawning after the last observed 00:44:05 event are unknown.

Of the 312 frontend-proxy 5xx log lines in the window only the newest 15 are visible, so per-route and per-status breakdowns of the proxy 5xx population (and whether any non-checkout routes contributed) are not established.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so there is no independent record of when the chaos Schedule or NetworkChaos objects were created or modified.

The exact request-level scope of the alert (which of the proxy's routes/statuses the rule counts) is unknown because its expression could not be read; the alert is described here only via the proxy's own error spans and access-log 500s.
next_steps: Read the Schedule chaos-mesh/otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition and one of its NetworkChaos children (spec.selector, spec.target, spec.direction, spec.duration, status.experiment.desiredPhase) to confirm which pod pairs are partitioned.

Confirm with the chaos owner whether this email/checkout network-partition schedule is an intended experiment; if not, suspend it and re-measure the frontend-proxy error-span rate against the 0.0037–0.0185/s baseline.
Load or fetch the RequestErrorRate alert rule expression and its data source to reconcile the annotated 0.6444 value with the span-derived error rates.
Add status tags and access logging to the email service so quote→email failures can be attributed per call.
